== Biography ==
Robert Finley Glasgow was born in Adams County, Ohio on 12 Apr 1820.<ref>* Faris, David, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (Baltimore, MD, Gateway Press, Inc., 1990), p. 82</ref>. He was married to Nancy Jane Campbell, daughter of Robert  & Ann Glasgow Campbell in 1847 in Adams County, Ohio.  He was a farmer in Scott Township, Adams County, Ohio in the 1860 and 1860 US Federal Censuses.<ref>1850 United States Federal Census for Robt F Glasgow</ref><ref>1860 United States Federal Census for Robert S Glasgow</ref>. In 1866 they sold their farm to James Allison and moved to Illinois.<ref>* Faris, David, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (Baltimore, MD, Gateway Press, Inc., 1990), p. 82 </ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Father and family evidence ===

Rosanna [[Finley-134|Finley]] is separately assessed as his mother at 93%, because the 1925 account explicitly calls her mother of Finley and Stuart. That identification shares the stated child-identity limits; the two parent percentages are not independent probabilities.

The 1 October 1926 [[Glasgow-2043|Samuel Steele interview]] explicitly names Finley’s father as Robert Glasgow, husband of [[Finley-134|Rosanna Finley]]. The Campbell wife, Robert/William/John/Nancy child group, Nancy’s Dr J. A. Glasgow marriage, and Illinois migration identify the Finley represented by [[Glasgow-16]]. Ora’s separate 1925 interview ties that same family to Robert Washington and the Weldon death. The named spouse selects [[Glasgow-8|Robert Barclay Glasgow]] rather than the older Robert-12/Rosannah Barclay couple. The 24 October 1925 recollection separately names Finley as a child of Robert and Rosanna Finley.<ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 18, pp. 259–260; Samuel Steele Glasgow interview, 1 October 1926; library transcription, PDF pp. 1619–1620. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=1619 Uniontown Public Library transcript]. Not a manuscript facsimile.</ref><ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 15, p. 101; Robert Arthur Glasgow household interview, 24 October 1925; library transcription, PDF p. 659. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=659 Uniontown Public Library transcript]. Not a manuscript facsimile.</ref><ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 15, pp. 310–313; Idelma Ora Glasgow interview, 3 November 1925; library transcription, PDF pp. 759–761. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=760 Uniontown Public Library transcript]. Not a manuscript facsimile.</ref>

The existing father is confidently assessed at 93%. 93% is a subjective confident assessment of the complete father–adult-profile identification, based on retrospective named testimony and family matching, not a contemporary birth record. Separate witnesses in one researcher’s transcript can share family tradition. The reported near-Peoria death is imprecise beside Weldon; the latter is retained. The exact 12 April 1820 birthday is NOT an identity anchor: the same source assigns it to the distinct [[Glasgow-2175|Iowa Robert Glasgow]]. All dates and other ancestry remain unchanged.


=== Earlier father review, 22 October 2026 — superseded below ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-8]] is assessed at 65% (probable). Robert Finley’s exact 1820 birth and Adams County family fit the selected Robert Barclay’s 1783 generation. The particular inherited household attribution is plausible within the compiled Glasgow family, but Robert Finley’s held biography and census references do not themselves name his father.

Probable 65%; specific existing family assignment, without a retained independent parent clause.

Next useful test: Read Robert Finley’s Faris entry and underlying family evidence.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-16 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-16]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
